audit.whatIsWrong: content 'mid' says 'respect the overheated Flamespitter' and whys[3] says 'he pokes with overheated Flamespitter'. Overheating is the state in which Rumble cannot cast Flamespitter at all.
audit.why: Junkyard Titan: 'When he reaches 50% Heat he reaches Danger Zone, granting all his basic abilities bonus effects. When he reaches 100% Heat, he starts Overheating, gaining bonus Attack Speed and granting his basic attacks bonus damage, but making him unable to cast spells for a few seconds.' Danger Zone is the empowered-poke state; Overheating is the spell-locked state. The text has these backwards, which inverts the single most important timing read in the lane — a player told to respect 'overheated Flamespitter' will back off during the exact window Rumble is defenceless. The same file's dontsFull[0] already says 'danger-zone Q' correctly, so the layers contradict each other.
audit.corrected: Danger Zone (50% Heat) is when Flamespitter is empowered. Overheating (100% Heat) locks him out of casting for several seconds and is your window to walk in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Wither is the direct counter to the Overheat state itself.
audit.why: While Overheating Rumble 'gains bonus Attack Speed and grants his basic attacks bonus damage' — his damage converts from spells to autos for that window. Wither's attack-speed component is therefore a targeted answer to Overheat, not just generic kiting. Both halves of the interaction are in the kit files and neither layer mentions it.
audit.corrected: When he Overheats his damage becomes auto-attack based; that is exactly when Wither's attack-speed slow does the most work.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer makes Scrap Shield the matchup-defining ability: breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid, loading ('Engage only on Scrap Shield's cooldown'), dosFull[0], focus, tldr, winCon and enemyWin all key off it.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is a 6-second cooldown at every rank. There is no meaningful window on a 6s cooldown — it is effectively always available, so 'engage only when Scrap Shield is down' is advice that can never be executed and will make a player stand still forever. enemyWin's 'Rumble wins by landing Scrap Shield' is also incoherent: it is a self-cast shield, nothing is landed. The real gate is the Heat bar, and the real long cooldown in the lane is The Equalizer at 130s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Re-key the entry off the Heat bar and The Equalizer's 130s cooldown instead of a 6s self-shield.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (W Scrap Shield CD 6; R The Equalizer CD 130/105/80)

audit.whatIsWrong: No range information, despite the lane being decided by who can touch whom.
audit.why: Electro Harpoon is 850 range, Wither is 700, Flamespitter is 600. Rumble can chip from outside the range of the only tool Nasus has, which is the concrete reason the early game is conceded. 'He just kites the slow' gestures at this without giving the player the numbers to act on.
audit.corrected: Electro Harpoon 850 > Wither 700 > Flamespitter 600 — he pokes from outside your only answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] writes 'Drop Equalizer'; the ability is The Equalizer.
audit.why: Flagged in the packet suspectNames and confirmed against the kit file. Minor, but it is the ability's actual name.
audit.corrected: Drop The Equalizer across the wave.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Equalizer's cooldown is never stated anywhere.
audit.why: 130/105/80 is the longest cooldown in the matchup by a wide margin. A Rumble who has used it for a wave clear or a bad teamfight has no zoning tool for over two minutes at rank 1 — that is the window for the splitpush the entry already recommends, and it is unstated.
audit.corrected: The Equalizer is 130s at rank 1 and 80s at rank 3 — after he spends it, take the side lane.

notes: Two things for you beyond the edits. (1) The 'overheated Flamespitter' error inverts Danger Zone and Overheating and is likely templated — worth grepping every lane for 'overheat' used to mean 'empowered', because it means the opposite. (2) DATA DEFECT in champ-data/_kits/rumble.json: Scrap Shield carries flags 'knockup' and 'terrain', which it does not have (it is a self-shield plus a move-speed burst, per Riot's own description in the same file). The Equalizer also carries 'terrain', but it creates a damage-and-slow zone, not collision terrain — it does not block paths or dashes. If any generator consumed those flags, other champions' Rumble entries may claim he knocks up or walls people off. I did not touch the kit file. I also left focus.letters alone even though it still reads ["W"] while focus.text now points at the passive — flipping it to ["P"] would match, but I did not want to guess how the UI consumes that array.
